requirement: Each file entry pairs its assigned root ID with the domain identity serialized as a JSON value. The whole entry is a valid node argument under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference.consistency`. Follow `next` to retrieve further pages.
rationale:
The subject's obligations are: (1) each file entry pairs its assigned root ID (`node`) with the domain identity serialized as JSON (`data`); (2) the whole entry works unchanged as a `node`+`data` argument under `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference.consistency`; (3) following `next` retrieves further pages. The consistency requirement is only cited, so I checked that the tests apply it to listed entries. I did not reassess its own tests.

**Entry shape and ID/data pairing**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[listing_continuations_return_complete_paths_from_the_original_listing]` lists 2000 files. For every entry on every page it deserializes `node` as a `NodeId`. It asserts `entry["data"]` equals the cache's `node_data` for that node. It also asserts the collected node IDs equal the interned IDs of the expected `item….rs#` identities, in order. So the ID is the assigned root ID and `data` is the serialized identity.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agent_uses_domain_source_tools_in_independent_executions]` is an end-to-end run. It asserts every listing entry has a `u64` `node` and a `u64` `data.id`.

**Whole entry is a valid node argument**
- The same configured test passes `listing["files"][selected_index]` unchanged, with both `node` and `data`, to `read_node`. It asserts the read returns `a source snapshot`. It also asserts the domain's recorded node-data reads for `visible/selected.txt` match the expected identity. This shows the combined entry is accepted and resolves to the right source.
- Rejection of mismatched, unassigned or malformed combinations belongs to `node_reference.consistency`, which is cited here. It needs no test under this subject.

**Pagination**
- The continuations test asserts the first page has `next`. It then follows `get_next_page` until `next` is absent. It adds a file after the first page and still gets the complete original listing. Dependencies stay empty on each page.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads]` also follows `next` for `list_sources` and checks that no reads are registered.

`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` covers which files are listed. That is outside this requirement's text. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_tools_forward_arguments_and_present_discovery_and_read_results]` uses the generic non-domain tool, whose entries are bare resources. It adds nothing here and does not contradict the subject.

I found no obligation in the text that the tests leave unasserted. The tests are marked with `{test}` references to this requirement.

text: Each file entry pairs its assigned root ID with the domain identity serialized as a JSON value. The whole entry is a valid node argument under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference.consistency`. Follow `next` to retrieve further pages.

A tool MUST also accept `node` and `data` together. Look up the existing ID and compare its stored identity with the deserialized `data` using `D::NodeData` equality. Use that ID on a match. An unassigned ID, malformed data, or a mismatch produces a tool error, even if the supplied data would be valid on its own. A `path` address may include `location` and must be used separately from `node` and `data`.
